justifications.c1: Only a statutory maximum (OSHA $16,550 per serious violation) and two UK fines (£50k Flowchem, search-confirmed; £100k Granville) for sites with NO shower, which a sensor does not fix; no injury cost or penalty tied to an un-flushed or faulty shower (recorded not found).
justifications.c2: Weekly activation duty per ANSI Z358.1 (ISHN, search-confirmed) and a mandatory monthly activation under Cal/OSHA 8 CCR 5162 (search-confirmed), with university weekly logs; the manual task recurs weekly per unit.
justifications.c3: Documented weekly manual routine (UNMC log, SafetyCulture template), paid local alarm kits (Haws 9001 $2,198–$4,795) and vendor service contracts; labour time per round is not quantified.
justifications.c4: Cal/OSHA 5162 requires monthly activation with documentation; OSHA 1910.151(c) requires facilities and was among the most-cited serious violations (slide-deck copy only) with repeat citations rising (ISHN); UK duty is only general COSHH and no insurer condition was found.
justifications.c5: EHS Manager adverts (Kelly, Jobot) explicitly assign eyewash/safety-shower inspections and records, and one (DSJ Global) mentions safety budget; US only, no UK advert.
justifications.c6: Hughes runs a service fleet visiting sites at 3/6/12-month intervals (vendor claim only) and Emerson integrators sell monitoring into large plants; no evidence that a site-visiting channel resells low-cost monitoring to SMEs.
justifications.c7: Willingness to pay is shown by Emerson/Honeywell/Apprion/Banner systems and the Haws alarm at $2,198+, plus a white paper on costly wired retrofits; gap at SME level is plausible but no subscription prices or complaints were found.
justifications.c8: Off-the-shelf LoRaWAN nodes exist (Dragino LSN50v2 $74, Milesight) and a flow switch can sense activation, but the BOM is near or above £50–60, clamp-on activation sensing is unproven here and some sites need ATEX/IECEx Zone 1/2 equipment.
justifications.c9: The weekly or monthly duty with documentation gives a structural reason for ongoing logging, but no comparable product's subscription price was found.
justifications.c10: Regulator sources (HSE press release, OSHA info sheet), trade press (ISHN) and a peer-reviewed contamination study; no first-hand practitioner complaints found.

weakest: No money figure is tied to the actual problem (an un-flushed or unseen-activation shower): the UK fines are for absent showers and the OSHA figure is only a statutory maximum, and no subscription pricing was found.
